title: DNA extraction protocol for the thraustochytrid Aurantiochytrium limacinum
author: Ben Leyland
materials: Scrape some colony using a plastic pipette tip.

Immediately remove PCR tube from thermocycler, and allow to cool to room temperature on the benchtop. [Room temperature cooling is important for several reasons. It allows for re-annealing of DNA to the more stable dsDNA form, as well as the precipitation of cellular debris.]

steps.title: Grow colonies on agar
steps.instruction: Incubate colonies on an agar‑media plate for 4 days; use colonies no older than 2 months.

steps.title: Add DNA Extraction Buffer
steps.instruction: Pipette 20 µL of DNA Extraction Buffer into a PCR tube.

steps.title: Resuspend colony in buffer
steps.instruction: Add a single colony to the tube and resuspend it in the 20 µL DNA Extraction Buffer.

steps.title: Heat lysate
steps.instruction: Place the tube at 95 °C for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Add sterile water and mix
steps.instruction: After cooling to room temperature, add sterile nuclease‑free deionized water and mix gently.

substeps.instruction: Filter‑sterilize the sterile nuclease‑free deionized water before use.
Add 80 µL of the water to the cooled lysate.
Mix gently by pipetting up and down.

steps.title: Centrifuge to pellet debris
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube to pellet cellular debris (speed and time as appropriate for your centrifuge).

steps.title: Store or use DNA extract
steps.instruction: The DNA extract is ready for downstream applications.

substeps.instruction: Use 1–2 µL of extract in a 50 µL PCR reaction.
If not used immediately, freeze at –20 °C.
For temporary storage, keep on ice, in ice water, or at 4 °C.
